current.text: He enters the season healthy after his first healthy offseason in years. He reportedly added 15 pounds of muscle.
Experts project him at about 33 minutes per game because he starts the season healthy.
Expected to play about 45 games, 50 at most. Mark also gave a lower guess of about 40 games.

Projected at around 20 to 25 points and about 10 rebounds per game, with occasional big scoring games. He is seen as an emergency scorer who gets to the free throw line and rebounds while teammates carry most of the scoring.
One expert expects more from him than last season, but keeps him outside the top 50 because of injury concerns.
Philadelphia added LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, who join Embiid and Tyrese Maxey. The projected starting five is Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Brown, James and Embiid.
Experts expect the four stars to cut into each other's usage, which caps Embiid's shots.
Mark projects Philadelphia at about 51 to 52 wins, with growing pains in October and November and load management for the stars.
The Sixers have only 13 back-to-backs this season, but three of them fall in the fantasy playoffs.
Factor the three playoff back-to-backs into his draft price, since he is not expected to play back-to-backs.
The experts agree he should not be drafted inside the top 50.

The experts disagree on his price after the top 50. Most call him a fair high-risk gamble around picks 56 to 64, and one expects him to finish in the 60s and calls his ESPN rank of 88 thievery. Josh would not touch him at all, and he went for 16 USD in an auction mock.
One expert gives the pick about a 10% chance of working out, but a big payoff if it does.

durable.text: He has repeated knee problems and surgeries. He is often listed as questionable and misses many games.
Experts have low hopes for his long-term health. Josh avoids him because of the knee history.
When he plays, his per game line is among the best in the league. He ranked 11th per game last season.
He is an elite scorer who gets to the free throw line. He makes a high share of a large number of free throws, so he lifts a team's FT% clearly.
He commits many turnovers, even for a center.
As an often-injured player, he is worth slightly more in roto than in head-to-head leagues like ours.
Nick Nurse plays his starters very heavy minutes.

note: He went for 24 USD in our last auction. Yahoo values him at 19 USD, but the average costs are only 7.4 USD (Yahoo) and 8.3 USD (ESPN), and an auction mock sold him for 16 USD. Since experts expect only 40 to 50 games, a price near the 8 to 16 USD range carries the risk better than last year's 24 USD. He fits punt TO builds that want FT% and points from a center. Early in the season, check how many games he plays, whether he sits every back-to-back, and how his shots hold up next to Maxey, LeBron James and Jaylen Brown. Remember that three Sixers back-to-backs fall in our playoff weeks.
